subject: Operational constraints for tenant isolation across EU & APAC private clusters
messages:
From: Michael Lopez <michael.lopez@acme.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: Acme Legal <acme-legal@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Tenant isolation / activation constraints for EU & APAC private deploy

Vanessa —

Thanks for the prep call last week. As we scope the Private deployment for Acme Financial I need a concise summary of constraints we should give our legal & ops teams. Specifically we need answers to the following so we can finalize the SOW: 

- Can Redwood guarantee tenant traffic for EU tenants will never egress to APAC clusters (routing, peering, DNS behavior)?
- Do you support region-bound KMS/HSM keys (i.e., separate keys and key material per region)?
- For failover, what exact activation window, DNS TTL, and expected RTO/RPO are realistic for a warm-stanby routing failover between sovereign clusters?
- Any limitations on transit gateway/BGP peering, IP ranges we must provide, or vendor VPNs that would prevent an on-prem connection to both regions?

Attached: ACME_requirements.xlsx (high level checklist). We need a short written response we can include in the procurement packet.

Also, can you confirm what logging/evidence we will receive for cross-region data movement (if any)? Our compliance team will need proof artifacts.

Best,
Michael Lopez
CTO, Acme Financial
attachment: ACME_requirements.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB)

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: Michael Lopez <michael.lopez@acme.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, Acme Legal <acme-legal@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Tenant isolation / activation constraints for EU & APAC private deploy

Michael —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by proposed next steps and attachments.

Short answers:
- Tenant isolation: Yes — we can enforce strict routing so EU tenant traffic is pinned to the EU private cluster. We use policy-based routing at the edge and per-tenant routing rules in the control plane; no cross-region application-layer egress will be initiated by Redwood for pinned workloads.
- KMS/HSM: Supported. We recommend region-specific CMKs/HSM partitions for EU and APAC. Customer-managed keys are also supported; we can integrate with your KMS/HSM via mutual TLS and IAM-based key policies.
- Failover & RTO/RPO: For a scripted warm activation across sovereign clusters we target an RTO of 10–30 minutes (DNS + canary routing + cache warmup) and RPO measured in seconds for ephemeral inference state (we persist only necessary tenant metadata). RTO depends on DNS TTL and your fronting DNS provider; we recommend a 60s TTL during cutover windows.
- Network constraints: We support TGW/transit hubs and BGP peering. You will need to supply the IP ranges for the on-prem egress and accept the peering ACLs. Vendor VPNs are fine; however, some appliances that block BGP or NAT hairpinning will require config changes.
- Evidence & logs: We will provide signed routing-change audit records, per-activation runbooks, and system-level flow logs showing ingress/egress interfaces for the activation window. For compliance, we can prepare a cutover attestation bundle (hash-signed) after each failover exercise.

Attachments: redwood-private-deploy-architecture.pdf (high-level topology), and a link to a shared drive with our templates.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical sync (30–45m) to capture your on-prem IPs, DNS provider, and KMS preferences (can do tomorrow).
2) We will map the KMS binding and generate an HSM-key-per-region proposal (Karthik to lead).
3) Run a lightweight failover simulation on a staging slice; we will produce the attestation bundle.

If that sounds good I will loop Karthik & Marissa and schedule the sync.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
attachment: redwood-private-deploy-architecture.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-redwood-private-templates

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Michael Lopez <michael.lopez@acme.com>, Acme Legal <acme-legal@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Tenant isolation / activation constraints for EU & APAC private deploy

Vanessa / Marissa —

Detail notes for the technical sync (pulling from Vanessa's summary):

1) Routing & peering
- We'll implement per-tenant routing via virtual network isolation; route tables will be scoped per-tenant and per-region. EU tenant prefixes will be advertised only to EU-facing transit attachments.
- BGP: we support eBGP between customer edge and our region transit with MD5 auth. Prefer ASN range: 650XX or your allocated private ASN.
- NAT/Egress: For EU pinned workloads we will NAT to EU egress IPs. No cross-region NAT unless explicit failover activation occurs.

2) DNS and TTLs
- For planned activation we'll use weighted DNS + health-check-driven routing via the transit LB. Recommend a baseline TTL of 300s for normal ops and 60s during cutover windows.

3) KMS/HSM
- Recommend separate HSM partitions per region. Customer-managed CMK recommended for highest assurance; otherwise Redwood-managed CMK per region with HSM-backed key material. We'll provide a kms-key-mapping.csv that maps tenant -> region -> key-id.

4) Evidence & attestation
- We will capture: routing-change audit (signed by control plane), VPC flow logs (region-labeled), and a post-cutover attestation PDF with SHA256 hashes. This bundle should satisfy most audit needs.

5) Failover runbook & tests
- Canary test: promote 5% of traffic to target region and validate inference fidelity and latency.
- Full activation: scriptable runbook that flips route advertisements, updates healthy-backend sets, and purges local caches. Expected checklist time: ~10–30m depending on external DNS propagation and cache warmup.

Questions for Acme (to confirm during sync):
- Which DNS provider will you use? (we need API creds or a maintenance window)
- Do you require separate HSM appliances in your data centers or will cloud HSMs suffice?

Attachments: peering-diagram.vsdx, kms-key-mapping.csv

-Karthik
Network & Infra Lead | Redwood Inference
attachment: peering-diagram.vsdx (vsdx, 480KB)
attachment: kms-key-mapping.csv (csv, 12KB)

From: Michael Lopez <michael.lopez@acme.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: Acme Legal <acme-legal@acme.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Tenant isolation / activation constraints for EU & APAC private deploy

Vanessa / Karthik —

Thanks — that is exactly the level of detail we need. Confirming the asks from our side for the sync:
- DNS provider: FastDNS (we will create a service account with API access for the maintenance window).
- KMS: We will require physically separate HSMs (on-prem appliances) in EU and APAC data centers; cloud HSM is not sufficient for EU-regulatory keys.
- We can provide IP ranges and an initial maintenance window Friday 2026-11-13 02:00–04:00 UTC for a staging failover exercise.

Also attaching the signed SOW so legal can move to PO.

Appreciate the clear runbook items. Please schedule the 30m tech sync and send an agenda.

Best,
Michael Lopez
CTO, Acme Financial
